candidates.title: 14 charged in $22.5 million cargo theft ring that stopped moving freight trains
candidates.excerpt: Federal prosecutors charged 14 people in an alleged $22.5 million cargo theft conspiracy targeting freight trains across Southern California. Nathan Daniel Angel, 21, of East Los Angeles, allegedly coordinated burglaries involving more than 70 shipping containers. The operation targeted Nike sneakers, Milwaukee tools, JBL electronics and other consumer products. Investigators traced shipments from railroad tracks to residential storage locations and commercial resale businesses. The defendants allegedly cut train air hoses to trigger emergency stops before removing valuable freight. Accomplices drove trucks and vans to predetermined locations, collected merchandise and transported it to nearby residences. Other participants inventoried products, negotiated prices and arranged deliveries to buyers. Prosecutors describe train burglaries spanning February 2024 through August 2026. candidates.excerpt: U.S. rail traffic rose 7.3% in the week ending November 14, 2026, compared with the same week last year, as double-digit intermodal growth outpaced gains in conventional carload shipments, according to the Association of American Railroads. Intermodal volume increased 10.7% year over year, while total carloads rose 3.3%, AAR said in a weekly update. Eight of the 10 carload commodity groups recorded gains. Motor vehicles and parts posted the strongest percentage increase among carload categories, rising 16.2%. Forest products followed with a 14% gain, while metallic ores and metals increased 10.7% and petroleum and petroleum products advanced 10.3%. The remaining categories posting increases were farm products excluding grain, and food, up 3.1%; chemicals, up 2.3%; nonmetallic minerals, up 2.1%; and coal, up 0.9%. Grain shipments fell 4.7%. candidates.title: NS CEO: UP merger is rail’s answer to the highway and autonomous trucks
candidates.excerpt: NEW YORK — Norfolk Southern CEO Mark George laid out the case for the proposed merger with Union Pacific on Thursday, Nov. 19, saying the deal will end two decades of market share loss to the highway while helping the transcontinental railroad fend off the threat of autonomous trucks. George, speaking at the RailTrends conference, noted that the big four U.S. Class I railroads lost volume from 2005 through 2025: NS traffic is down 9%, CSX 14%, UP 12%, and BNSF 4%. Part of this decline, he said, came as the industry adopted the low-cost Precision Scheduled Railroading operating model over the past decade. “Railroads really shifted their focus to efficiency over growth. And that was very effective,” George said. “We all became a lot more efficient, but there was no growth. And since 2020, even after the economic recovery, rail volumes actually dropped.” Now autonomous trucking is accelerating, George said, with fleet rollouts expected over the next three years. candidates.excerpt: PSA Singapore has started construction of the second phase of Tuas Port, marking a major milestone in the expansion of Singapore’s container port infrastructure. The development will add 21 mega berths and 8.6 kilometres of wharf. The new berths will have a water depth of 23 metres, allowing them to accommodate the world’s largest container vessels. Phase Two is the largest of Tuas Port’s four development phases in terms of wharf length. Operations are expected to begin gradually from 2028. The expansion aims to strengthen Singapore’s position as a global container transshipment hub and support growing demand for efficient cargo handling. Automation to play a central role PSA plans to expand the use of automation and artificial intelligence across the new terminal facilities. Once Phase Two is completed, nearly 1,000 autonomous Intelligent Guided Vehicles (IGVs) will move containers around the terminal. candidates.title: From Fragmented Plans to Superintelligent Terminals
candidates.excerpt: Container terminals face growing pressure to move more cargo, turn vessels around faster and control costs within existing infrastructure. Yet even terminals with sophisticated planning tools can struggle when berth scheduling, vessel stowage, yard allocation and equipment dispatch operate independently. A plan that works for one department may create congestion, delays or unnecessary moves elsewhere. The opportunity lies in connecting these decisions through integrated, AI-driven planning, clear visualisation and turning operational information into actionable knowledge. Turning information into knowledge Information alone does not create understanding. candidates.title: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom
candidates.excerpt: Private credit gains ground in Asia amid AI boom Private credit is gaining ground in Asia as demand for flexible capital grows and the AI boom needs funding, according to KKR. Asia has historically relied on banks for credit, and they still provide 88 per cent of the region’s debt capital, compared with 50 per cent in Europe and just 31 per cent in the US. However, forces reshaping Japan and driving investment in AI infrastructure are starting to change this, KKR said in a recent blog post. In the US and Europe, regulators have made banks retrench, but that is not happening in Asia. Instead, private credit is in demand across the region because it offers flexible capital alongside banks that remain deeply embedded in corporate financing. KKR argued that Asian banks provide cheap but inflexible capital, and that private credit was plugging this gap. The Amsterdam-based fintech business, which serves 300,000 businesses, has introduced a business overdraft and credit card, offering personalised limits of up to €20,000 (£16,700) and €40,000, respectively. Finom said more than half of its customers now qualify for credit under the new offering, compared with between 11 per cent and 17 per cent under its previous credit product. (NASDAQ: RAIL) (“FreightCar America” or the “Company”), a diversified manufacturer and supplier of railroad freight cars, railcar parts and components, today reported results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026. Third quarter results were consistent with the preliminary results the Company announced on October 19, 2026. Akiem Hicks
candidates.excerpt: Akiem Hicks was an interior defensive lineman for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers who earned a 61.9 overall PFF defensive grade in the 2022 season, 60th among 127 qualified interior defensive linemans. His PFF pass-rush grade of 58.5 ranked 83rd among 127 qualified interior defensive linemans. His run-defense grade of 65.7 ranked 34th at the position. He generated 8 total pressures as a pass rusher. That total included 1 sacks, 4 hurries, 3 hits. Against the run, he recorded 15 solo tackles.
